findings.failureScenario: `cargo xtask corpus --download` runs curl with no --connect-timeout/--max-time/--retry, writing straight into the final path. A stalled connection hangs the command indefinitely; a mid-transfer failure leaves a truncated file at `out`. The `?` aborts the whole run, and the next run sees `out.exists()`, skips the download, fails the sha256 check, deletes the file and errors again; only the third run actually re-downloads. One transient network error therefore costs two failed runs, and one bad sample stops every later sample from being fetched.
findings.action: Pass --connect-timeout, --max-time and --retry to curl, download to `<name>.part` and rename after the sha256 matches, and keep going after a failed sample, reporting all failures at the end.

findings.failureScenario: The script creates a keychain at a fixed path ($TMP/lightcraft-signing.keychain-db), prepends it to the user's keychain search list, and its EXIT trap removes only the .p12. If the script is run again on a machine whose TMP persists (a self-hosted runner or a local run), `security create-keychain` fails because the file exists and `set -e` aborts the signing job. Any failure after line 36 also leaves the temporary keychain on the search list.
findings.action: Delete any stale keychain (`security delete-keychain "$KEYCHAIN" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$KEYCHAIN"`) before creating it, and have the EXIT trap restore the original search list and delete the keychain on failure.
